text:
Amelia (PM): Quick sync — now that v1 is live, we need a concrete plan for the next 3 sprints: balancing customer-reported bugs vs high-impact enhancements. Proposing a 'banding' cadence: Sprint A=bug band (50-60% capacity to critical/sev2), Sprint B=feature wave (70% enhancements), repeat. Thoughts?
Jorge (Eng): +1 to a pattern. Curious about how we classify 'critical' vs 'heat' from support. Can we get a list of top 10 signals? @Rina
Rina (Support): sending list in a sec. Top signals: streaming timeout, dev console 500s, regen correctness for snippets, embeddings mismatch. Customers with active contracts: 6 accounts impacted.
Amelia (PM): ok thanks. Proposal: for bug band sprints we reserve 2 full squads and 1 small squad for platform SRE items (latency, KV cache regressions). For feature waves, 2 squads on features, 1 on carry-forward bugs. Is that feasible? @Jorge
Jorge (Eng): Feasible if we freeze non-critical infra changes. SRE work can be scoped to <3 day tasks per ticket, otherwise will spill. We should define a clear acceptance criteria for what goes into bug band.
Devon (SRE): Agree. Acceptance criteria for bug band items: reproducible in prod or affects SLA (>5% error or >20% latency regression on p95) or security/availability. We'll add runbook updates as part of ticket.
Kai (Design): For feature waves, design can deliver scoped flows for two features per sprint, with prototypes. We should avoid mid-sprint pivots — prefer blocking design signoff at sprint start. I'll list deliverables per feature.
Mark (PMM): From customer signals, prioritise enhancements that reduce support volume (e.g., clearer error messaging, retry UX). Those tend to show ROI quickly. Can we tag improvements with expected Delta-Support %?
Amelia (PM): Good idea — tag tickets with estimated Support Impact and Revenue Risk. That helps tradeoffs during grooming. Also: rollout milestones — we should use canary + 24h metrics window and rollback triggers: 2x error rate or 20% latency p95 increase in canary traffic.
Jorge (Eng): +1 to rollback triggers. For canary, suggest staged ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 50% over 12h with metrics checks at each step.
Rina (Support): We'll prepare a customer comms template for both bug band fixes and feature waves. Also need a KB update checklist in ticket definition.
Amelia (PM): Action items: 1) @Rina share top signals doc (due today). 2) @Jorge scope runbook + estimate squads for band vs wave (due EOD tomorrow). 3) @Kai produce design signoff checklist and prototypes for two candidate features (due Wed). 4) @Mark produce expected Support Impact tags for candidate features (due Wed). I'll run weekly banding prioritization meeting Friday at 10am. 
Devon (SRE): We'll also add automated p95 latency dashboards for each route and alert on canary windows.
Jorge (Eng): Quick Q: how do we treat medium-sev bugs that block big customers but are low occurrence? Do they go into bug band or triaged into feature wave with higher priority?
Amelia (PM): Treat by customer risk: if a paying customer is blocked (contract > threshold) we escalate into the current sprint as a quick patch. Otherwise medium can backlog into bug band. We'll track exceptions as 'escalations' in sprint board.
Mark (PMM): Suggest adding a 'fast-follow' tag for features that can be toggled on/off and are safe to ship during feature waves; that reduces rollback blast radius.
Kai (Design): Noted, will add feature toggle checklist to design signoff.
Amelia (PM): Thanks all — I'll update the roadmap doc and post the sprint allocation matrix after @Jorge shares capacity. Ping me if anything else.
Rina (Support): uploaded top-signals.csv to #files, link: https://redwood.infra/files/top-signals.csv :thumbsup: 
Jorge (Eng): Got it. I'll post squad estimates tomorrow.
Amelia (PM): Closing loop: final decision — adopt banding cadence starting next planning cycle, with the acceptance and rollback criteria above. We'll revisit after two cycles. :white_check_mark:
